proof:
Applying 4e868f774de77608 to the body $[0,1]\times K$ at a fixed base gives concavity and upper semicontinuity of $\delta_K^{1/d}$ on $K$. Thus $\widehat K$ is compact and convex, and it has interior since a ball inside $K$ gives a uniform positive depth lower bound on a smaller concentric ball. At a point of $\partial K$ an outward closed supporting halfspace intersects $K$ in a subset of its supporting hyperplane and captures zero $d$-volume. The graph image therefore has height zero and lies on $\partial\widehat K$.

Fix $x_0\in\operatorname{int}K$. For each $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ the homothetic copy $x_0+(1-\varepsilon)(K-x_0)$ lies in $\operatorname{int}K$, as seen by mixing each point of $K$ with an interior ball at $x_0$. Hence $|\partial K|_d\le(1-(1-\varepsilon)^d)|K|_d$, which tends to zero. The graph rim is an isometric copy of $\partial K$ in a $d$-plane and has zero $\mathcal H_d$ measure. Its complement carries zero mass of the pushforward, proving singularity. For an interval the height is the shorter endpoint distance, so its hypograph is a triangle with the two graph images among its vertices.

statement: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact full-dimensional convex body, $d\ge1$. Write $\delta_K(x)$ for its raw ordinary halfspace depth, using $d$-volume on $K$, and $\widehat K=\{(x,r):x\in K,\ 0\le r\le\delta_K(x)^{1/d}\}$. The graph map $x\mapsto (x,\delta_K(x)^{1/d})$ sends $\partial K$ to $\partial K\times\{0\}\subset\partial\widehat K$. That rim has $\mathcal H_d$ measure zero. Consequently the pushforward of every nonzero finite positive Borel measure carried by $\partial K$ is singular with respect to $\mathcal H_d$ on $\partial\widehat K$. For each interval in the three-interval example, the two endpoints lift to two vertices of the triangular hypograph and carry zero lifted boundary length.
title: Boundary measures lift to a singular rim of the own-depth hypograph
